Hero Licensing System.text: Only licensed heroes may use their Quirks in public as a profession: to fight villains, carry out rescues and act in emergencies. The Hero Public Safety Commission issues every license. A full hero license usually follows graduation from an accredited hero course and the Commission's requirements; a provisional license, earned through a separate exam, gives students limited emergency authority while they train. Every licensed hero registers a hero name with the Commission. The name is public and becomes the hero's working identity: costume, agency, merchandise and news coverage all use it, and many heroes keep their legal names out of the press. Hero Course students choose their hero names in class during their first year, and some change them later. A license is a legal status, not a rank. It allows a hero to use their Quirk on duty, to restrain and detain suspects until the police arrive and to direct civilians in an emergency. It does not allow punishment of suspects, unnecessary force or investigations beyond the hero's role, and heroes answer for misconduct the same way other public officials do. The Commission can suspend or revoke a license for criminal acts, reckless damage, serious misconduct or failure to meet its standards, and a hero who loses a license loses the legal right to work. Licensed heroes also carry duties: reporting incidents, cooperating with the police and keeping their registered information current.
